The Texas MSW landfills plan was submitted to fulfill the State's obligations under CAA section 111(d) to implement and enforce the requirements under the MSW Landfills EG. The EPA is approving the State plan and amending the agency regulations in accordance with the requirements of the CAA.

items.summary: The Department of Health and Human Services (HHS or "Department") is issuing this final rule to modify the Standards for Privacy of Individually Identifiable Health Information ("Privacy Rule") under the Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act of 1996 (HIPAA) and the Health Information Technology for Economic and Clinical Health (HITECH) Act. These modifications address standards that may impede the nationwide transition to value-based health care by limiting or discouraging individual access or care coordination and case management or posing other unnecessary burdens. The modifications in this final rule promote the essential sharing of individuals' protected health information (PHI) for care coordination and individual engagement while continuing to protect its privacy and security.
items.title: HIPAA Privacy Rule: Changes To Support Coordinated Care and Individual Engagement and Reduce Regulatory Burdens

The SIP revisions address reasonably available control technology (RACT) requirements for the 2008 and 2015 ozone national ambient air quality standards (NAAQS) relating to control technique guidelines (CTGs) for volatile organic compounds (VOC) via previously adopted CTG regulations, three new CTG regulations and permits for four facilities covered by the CTG for the Manufacture of High-Density Polyethylene, Polypropylene, and Polystyrene Resins respectively. The EPA is approving these revisions to the Pennsylvania SIP in accordance with the requirements of the Clean Air Act (CAA).
items.title: Air Plan Approval; Reasonably Available Control Technology (RACT) for Volatile Organic Compounds (VOC) Control Technique Guidelines (CTG) Under the 2008 and 2015 Ozone National Ambient Air Quality Standards (NAAQS)

items.summary: The Securities and Exchange Commission ("Commission") is proposing amendments to its executive and director compensation disclosure rules to make the requirements more principles-based and to reduce compliance burdens for registrants, while maintaining the disclosure of material information to investors. The proposed amendments would focus the disclosures on the principal executive officer ("PEO") and principal financial officer ("PFO"), streamline the tabular disclosure requirements, and simplify and rationalize various other aspects of the compensation disclosure rules, including the Compensation Discussion and Analysis ("CD&A"), pay ratio, pay- versus-performance, and perquisites disclosure requirements.
items.title: Executive Compensation Disclosure Reform

items.summary: This notice announces the inpatient hospital deductible and the hospital and extended care services coinsurance amounts for services furnished in calendar year (CY) 2027 under Medicare's Hospital Insurance Program (Medicare Part A). The Medicare statute specifies the formulae used to determine these amounts. For CY 2027, the inpatient hospital deductible will be $1,776. The daily coinsurance amounts for CY 2027 will be as follows: $444 for the 61st through 90th day of hospitalization in a benefit period; $888 for lifetime reserve days; and $222 for the 21st through 100th day of extended care services in a skilled nursing facility in a benefit period.
items.title: Medicare Program; CY 2027 Inpatient Hospital Deductible and Hospital and Extended Care Services Coinsurance Amounts

items.summary: This notice announces Medicare's Hospital Insurance Program (Medicare Part A) premium for uninsured enrollees in calendar year (CY) 2027. This premium is paid by enrollees aged 65 and over who are not otherwise eligible for benefits under Medicare Part A (hereafter known as the "uninsured aged") and by certain individuals with disabilities who have exhausted other entitlement. The monthly Medicare Part A premium for the 12 months beginning January 1, 2027 for these individuals will be $597. The premium for certain other individuals as described in this notice will be $328.
items.title: Medicare Program; CY 2027 Part A Premiums for the Uninsured Aged and for Certain Disabled Individuals Who Have Exhausted Other Entitlement

items.summary: This notice announces the monthly actuarial rates for aged (age 65 and over) and disabled (under age 65) beneficiaries enrolled in Part B of the Medicare Supplementary Medical Insurance (SMI) program beginning January 1, 2027. In addition, this notice announces the monthly premium for aged and disabled beneficiaries, the deductible for 2027, and the income-related monthly adjustment amounts to be paid by beneficiaries with modified adjusted gross income above certain threshold amounts. The monthly actuarial rates for 2027 are $418.70 for aged enrollees and $452.40 for disabled enrollees. The standard monthly Part B premium rate for all enrollees for 2027 is $209.40, which is equal to 50 percent of the monthly actuarial rate for aged enrollees (or approximately 25 percent of the expected average total cost of Part B coverage for aged enrollees). The 2027 premium is 3.2 percent or $6.50 higher than the 2026 standard premium rate of $202.90. The Part B deductible for 2027 is $292.00 for all Part B beneficiaries. If a beneficiary has to pay an income-related monthly adjustment amount, that individual will have to pay a total monthly premium of about 35, 50, 65, 80, or 85 percent of the total cost of Part B coverage. Beginning in 2023, certain Medicare enrollees who are 36 months post kidney transplant, and therefore no longer eligible for full Medicare coverage, can elect to continue Part B coverage of immunosuppressive drugs by paying a premium. For 2027, the immunosuppressive drug premium is $125.70.
items.title: Medicare Program; Medicare Part B Monthly Actuarial Rates, Premium Rates, and Annual Deductible Beginning January 1, 2027
